statements: On the UDA task, SPG significantly improves both detectors across all object categories of interest and at all difficulty levels.
In the target domain, we name this phenomenon as the “missing point” problem.

A naive approach is to randomly down-sample the point cloud but this not only fails to satisfactorily simulate the pattern of missing points (Figure 2d) but also hurts the performance on the source domain.
However, those methods have a limited capability in recovering the 3D shape of very partially observed objects.

solution.summary: In this paper, we investigate unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for LiDAR-based 3D object detection. To address this issue, we present Semantic Point Generation (SPG), a general approach to enhance the reliability of LiDAR detectors against domain shifts.
solution.approach: In this paper, we investigate unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for LiDAR-based 3D object detection.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we investigate unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for LiDAR-based 3D object detection.
To address this issue, we present Semantic Point Generation (SPG), a general approach to enhance the reliability of LiDAR detectors against domain shifts.
In this paper, we address the domain gap caused by the deteriorating point cloud quality and aim to improve 3D object detection in the setting of unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA).

experiments.summary: To validate the wide applicability of SPG, we experiment with two representative detectors, PointPillars [25] and PV-RCNN [49]. Combined with PV-RCNN [49], SPG achieves state-of-the-art 3D detection results on KITTI.

evidence.quote: To validate the wide applicability of SPG, we experiment with two representative detectors, PointPillars [25] and PV-RCNN [49].
Combined with PV-RCNN [49], SPG achieves state-of-the-art 3D detection results on KITTI.

applications.detail: Abstract In autonomous driving, a LiDAR-based object detector should perform reliably at different geographic locations and under various weather conditions.

deploymentClaims: Abstract In autonomous driving, a LiDAR-based object detector should perform reliably at different geographic locations and under various weather conditions.
Introduction A robust autonomous driving system requires its LiDAR-based detector to reliably handle different environmental conditions, e.g., geographic locations and weather conditions.

To demonstrate the wide applicability of SPG, we choose two representative detectors: 1) PointPillars [25], popular among industrialgrade autonomous driving systems; 2) PV-RCNN [49], a high performance LiDAR-based 3D detector [18, 54].
